Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Young female presents with acute lower abdominal pain (midline), increased urinary frequency, mild hematuria (pink urine), mild nausea (no vomiting), and sensation of being hot/sweaty.
- No urinary pain, no back pain, no fever (measured temperature ~37°C), no abnormal vaginal discharge.
- Past medical history non-contributory; drinks alcohol regularly but modestly; non-smoker.
- Family history: Mother had breast cancer (cured).
- Impression based on transcript and DDx is an uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI/cystitis) given constellation of urinary and constitutional symptoms and lack of severe systemic findings.
- Differential diagnoses considered include renal/urinary tract stone (less likely given absence of colicky/severe pain and back/flank symptoms), and less likely gynecologic or interstitial cystitis causes (no chronicity or gynecologic symptoms).
- Patient was prescribed a 3-day course of antibiotics (antibiotic name and dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript; transcript notes "twice a day for three days").
- Safety-net advice provided: return if worsening pain, fever, new symptoms, or recurrence.
- No physical examination or laboratory investigations documented.

Management Plan
- Prescribed a 3-day course of antibiotics for presumed UTI (antibiotic, dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Safety-netting instruction: Contact for review if pain worsens, high temperature develops, new symptoms arise, or if symptoms recur.
- Prescription to be sent to nominated pharmacy.
- No further investigations or referrals documented.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI/cystitis): High likelihood. Justified by classic presentation (acute lower abdominal pain, urinary frequency, mild hematuria, mild constitutional symptoms) and supported by both transcript and DDx.
- Renal/urinary tract stones: Moderate likelihood. Considered due to hematuria and pain but less likely given pain is not colicky/severe and absence of back/flank symptoms.
- Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome: Low likelihood. Chronicity, lack of hematuria, and young age reduce likelihood; acute onset less consistent.
